_comment: Annotated example. One of these per project, listing the full cast. Copy, rename to cast_scale.json, fill in real registration paths and director-declared proportions.
world_unit: define your project's baseline here, e.g. 'protagonist's standing height = 1.0'
_world_unit_comment: A single sentence defining what 1.0 world_height_units means for this project. Every other actor's proportion is declared relative to that baseline.
_tolerance_comment: How far (in percent) an actor's measured px-per-world-unit is allowed to deviate from the cast mean before cast-scale fails. Tune per project, but don't set this so loose it stops catching real mistakes.

actors.name: protagonist
actors._registration_comment: Path (relative to this file) to that actor's registration.json — must have a frame marked canonical:true with a scale_reference.

actors.name: example-huge-character
actors._comment_on_this_entry: A large ratio like this is a legitimate, intentional design choice — the check exists to verify the SOURCE ART actually matches this declared ratio, not to flag big size differences as errors.
